chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

«If a virgin is divorced three times and marains in a marriage that is not a full marriage (i.e., without consummation), she has become permanently divorced (khula') and is not permissible for her husband «until she marries a different husband»». Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And these narrations indicate what we said, that whoever divorces his wife three times for the sake of the Sunnah, she is not permissible to him until she marries a different husband, because the 'iddah divorce does not occur in the case of a virgin and one not fully married to him, and we have clarified that among the conditions of the 'iddah divorce is the return (muraja'ah) and the sexual intercourse after it, and both do not occur in the case of one not fully married to him, as we have clarified.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And likewise, whoever divorces a young girl who has not reached menstruation, even if he has had intercourse with her, if she is not of the age at which she menstruates; and whoever divorces a woman past the age of menstruation, that is also her ruling.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of triple divorce for a virgin or a woman not fully married to her husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates on the principle that for a virgin or a woman with whom consummation has not occurred, a single divorce counts as three because the prerequisite for a revocable divorce—consummation followed by return—is absent. This ruling is extended to pre-pubescent girls and menopausal women, highlighting the juristic consensus that the structural conditions of 'iddah' divorce do not apply when physical intimacy is lacking or impossible. This establishes a clear distinction between the procedural requirements for revocable versus irrevocable divorce in Shia fiqh.
